item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-d29f5588c6484f92","start_unit":134,"end_unit":138,"fact_summary":"Mexico's biosecurity framework is presented as grounded in national law, the Cartagena Protocol, the precautionary principle, and protection of health, biodiversity, food, and vulnerable groups; the document identifies unresolved needs for scientific risk assessment, risk classification, public technical information, interinstitutional coordination, and monitoring. It also describes 2019–2024-era measures including glyphosate and genetically modified maize actions, an Indigenous consultation protocol, maize traceability work, and biodiversity targets.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.4","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","3B.7","5B.7","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Partly relevant to 2023 through described prior-administration actions and inherited conditions, but the document itself is a 2026-2030 program and includes later legal and institutional developments.","ruler_attribution":"The document attributes the prior biosecurity advances to the preceding administration and CIBIOGEM, without naming López Obrador in these units.","limitations":["The source is retrospective and prospective rather than a contemporaneous 2023 evaluation.","It does not establish implementation quality or outcomes for López Obrador personally."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d29f5588c6484f92","start_unit":143,"end_unit":150,"fact_summary":"The proposed biosecurity policy would establish independent multidisciplinary expert committees, systematic expert and international reviews, standardized risk protocols, regional and species-specific assessments, long-term post-release monitoring, integrated traceability databases, public reporting, consultation, and adaptive management. The stated rationale is that existing policy requires more technical, comprehensive, verifiable, and proportionate implementation.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","3B.7","4B.6","5B.7","6B.5","6B.8","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Primarily post-2023 policy design; it identifies safeguards and gaps relevant to assessing the inherited 2023 posture but does not prove that the proposed measures were implemented in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"No direct attribution to López Obrador; the measures are assigned to SECIHTI, CIBIOGEM, and participating agencies under the later program.","limitations":["Most content concerns planned 2026-2030 actions.","The source does not provide a 2023 baseline for all safeguards or evidence of correction of identified failures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d29f5588c6484f92","start_unit":150,"end_unit":160,"fact_summary":"Biosecurity monitoring indicators show a 2024 baseline of 30% of resolutions and opinions evaluated by independent multidisciplinary technical committees and 40% incorporating systematic expert reviews and international comparisons; both have a 2030 target of 90%, while no 2025 progress is reported because the indicators are biennial.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","5B.7","6B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The measured baseline is 2024, outside the target 2023 period; it nevertheless indicates that formal expert-review coverage was incomplete immediately after the period.","ruler_attribution":"The indicators are attributed to SECIHTI and the Executive Secretariat of CIBIOGEM, not directly to López Obrador.","limitations":["No 2023 value is supplied.","The indicators measure formal evaluation coverage, not substantive safety outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d29f5588c6484f92","start_unit":183,"end_unit":201,"fact_summary":"Later biosecurity indicators record partial implementation: 40% alignment with the Cartagena Protocol, 31% integration of Nagoya access-and-benefit mechanisms, 35% operation of long-term post-release monitoring programs, and 40% operation of integrated interoperable information systems, all with targets of roughly 90–95% by 2030.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.4","1B.9","1B.10","4B.6","5B.7","6B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"These are 2024–2025 baselines from a later program, not direct 2023 observations; they provide contextual evidence of incomplete institutionalization after the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The indicators are attributed to SECIHTI and CIBIOGEM rather than directly to López Obrador.","limitations":["The source does not identify which shortcomings existed during 2023.","Targets are prospective and cannot establish achieved outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d29f5588c6484f92","start_unit":20,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"The later official diagnosis states that research remained weakly connected to public and productive-sector needs; only 0.06% of 2020–2024 Mexican scientific articles came from private-sector-affiliated researchers, and only 1% of 2002–2018 science-and-technology funding addressed selected social priorities such as poverty, inequality, inclusion, housing, security, and development. Mexico also remained technologically dependent, although 2023 high-technology-goods exports exceeded imports, producing a coverage ratio of 1.15.","question_ids":["1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.1","6B.5","6B.10","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence spans 2002–2024 and includes a 2023 trade indicator; it is contextual rather than a clean López Obrador-year attribution.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes national and historical conditions and does not directly attribute the cited outcomes to López Obrador.","limitations":["The funding figures predate 2023 and the research share covers 2020–2024.","The high-technology trade result is an aggregate outcome with multiple causal factors."]},{"source_id":"SRC-abca4cb2bc164975","start_unit":4,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL defines extreme poverty as income below the extreme-income poverty line plus at least three social deprivations. Between 2018 and 2022, multidimensional poverty fell from 41.9% to 36.3%, about 5.1 million fewer people, but extreme poverty slightly increased from 7.0% to 7.1%; the report frames eradication as a government priority and recommends targeted interventions for highly deprived groups.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.7","5B.8","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The comparison covers 2018–2022, ending before 2023; it is the closest outcome baseline supplied for evaluating the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The source reports national outcomes during the López Obrador administration but does not assign causal responsibility to him.","limitations":["No 2023 outcome is provided.","The report does not isolate federal policy effects from external, subnational, or household factors."]},{"source_id":"SRC-abca4cb2bc164975","start_unit":23,"end_unit":27,"fact_summary":"In 2022, extreme-poverty social deprivation was concentrated in social security access (97.2%), health-service access (81.7%), basic housing services (67.3%), food (50.5%), educational lag (46.1%), and housing quality (39.8%). Health-service deprivation rose from 25.6% in 2018 to 81.7% in 2022 amid institutional reconfiguration; among those seeking care, substantial shares used private facilities or pharmacy clinics rather than public services.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The evidence is for 2022, immediately preceding the target year, and provides a baseline of unresolved service-access problems.","ruler_attribution":"The source links the health-access increase to institutional reconfiguration but does not directly assign blame to López Obrador.","limitations":["The document does not establish whether conditions improved or worsened during 2023.","Some service-use estimates carry reduced statistical precision."]},{"source_id":"SRC-abca4cb2bc164975","start_unit":42,"end_unit":43,"fact_summary":"In 2022, 45.1% of the 9.1 million people in extreme poverty lived in households reporting no monetary social program; those without programs had higher health and food-access deprivation than recipients in several comparisons.","question_ids":["5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.7","6B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The evidence is from 2022 and serves as a pre-2023 baseline for coverage and targeting.","ruler_attribution":"The source reports program receipt and deprivation patterns without attributing them directly to López Obrador.","limitations":["Program receipt is observational and does not prove program effects.","No 2023 coverage data are supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-abca4cb2bc164975","start_unit":62,"end_unit":66,"fact_summary":"The proposed post-2024 poverty strategy combines pensions, disability support, child and education benefits, higher real minimum wages, and universal primary-care ambitions; CONEVAL notes that a cash transfer alone would not secure social rights. For older adults in extreme poverty, 82.1% lacked health-service access, and 79.6% of poor older-adult program beneficiaries still had that deprivation in 2022.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.9","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The policy proposals are for the subsequent administration, while the deprivation evidence is 2022; the source is not direct evidence of López Obrador's 2023 implementation.","ruler_attribution":"The proposals are attributed to the incoming administration and Claudia Sheinbaum, not López Obrador.","limitations":["This source cannot establish 2023 execution or outcomes.","The older-adult figures describe correlation between program receipt and deprivation, not program failure causation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-abca4cb2bc164975","start_unit":108,"end_unit":114,"fact_summary":"CONEVAL's principal findings identify persistent extreme-poverty burdens in 2022: 9.1 million people, high rural incidence, disproportionate impacts on Indigenous people, children, women, and disabled people, near-universal lack of social security among several target groups, and 784,000 children aged 3–17 out of school. The report recommends combining transfers with direct expansion of health, social-security, housing, food, and employment protections.","question_ids":["5B.7","5B.8","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.8","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The findings are 2022 baseline evidence immediately preceding 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates national conditions without directly assigning responsibility to López Obrador.","limitations":["No 2023 results or implementation records are included.","Recommendations are not evidence that the proposed measures were enacted."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied documents are primarily 2024–2026 retrospective or prospective policy documents and 2022 outcome baselines, so direct evidence specifically for López Obrador in calendar year 2023 is limited.","No supplied document materially addresses international peace, domestic violence, political freedom, or personal integrity questions beyond indirect institutional and social-policy context.","The official biosecurity document is titled as an animal-health/biosecurity strategy but contains extensive later science, innovation, and biotechnology programs; its post-2023 institutional references must not be treated as 2023 actions by López Obrador."]}
